sentences.text: Aymberedactylus is a genus of tapejarid pterosaur identified by its toothless jaw and a dentary symphysis making up half the jaw length.
Small neurovascular foramina on the jaw suggest the animal likely had a horned sheath over the tip of its jaw, and the preserved portion of the holotype mandible is 270 mm long.
It is distinguished by a long retroarticular process indicating good jaw control and a unique combination of traits including a deep shelf on the jaw symphysis and a relatively weak bite.
The preserved specimen is estimated to have had a wingspan of approximately 2 meters, and because the skull bones were not fully fused, it was likely a subadult.
The genus name Aymberedactylus comes from the Tupi word for "small lizard" and the Greek word for "finger," while the species name refers to the Brazilian state of Ceará.
A unique combination of traits includes a deep shelf on the jaw symphysis and a short, shallow dentary fossa indicating a relatively weak bite.
Aymberedactylus was discovered in the Aptian-Albian Crato Formation and described in 2016.
A 2016 phylogenetic analysis recovered Aymberedactylus as the most basal tapejarine.
Aymberedactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 108 million years ago, in what is now South America, specifically between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
